What the app shows you.

Sign in with your email, practise on one small room, then check the saved route before you send anything.

Screens from the current build in the iOS Simulator; on a real iPhone the camera fills the capture screen. The app is in invite-only testing through TestFlight.

One property, five steps.

  1. Agree the space and scope.

    After your initial enquiry, agree the rooms, approximate size, private areas to exclude and who reviews. One walkthrough covers up to 8 rooms of one property, counted automatically from your capture; each further 8 rooms uses one more. Keep street addresses and access instructions out of the public form.

  2. Prepare and capture.

    Clear personal documents and screens, keep people and pets out of the route, and keep lighting steady. Walk the space with the phone upright and follow the capture guidance. Review the saved photographs and route checks before leaving; those checks do not prove capture quality. After you send it, an automatic quality check assesses capture quality.

  3. Automatic processing and quality check.

    In the current app, open the saved capture and choose Export capture. Save the ZIP to Files or AirDrop it to your Mac, then use the private transfer route agreed with Veylet. This website does not yet have a capture-upload form. Veylet reconstructs it automatically, and an automatic quality check tests photo match, coverage, stray artefacts and walkable paths; no person checks it, and recording on the phone does not create a finished tour by itself. It is usually ready for your review within 1–2 hours of the upload finishing. Keep originals until the transfer is confirmed. A capture that is not good enough is never counted: the check retries once, then names the rooms to recapture.

  4. Review before sharing.

    Open the owner preview on your phone. Check every room, turns, doorways, floor and ceiling edges, privacy and phone navigation. Approve it or send one consolidated list of corrections. Each accepted walkthrough counts toward the 6 included in your free months, or toward your plan’s allowance after them. Capture permission and permission to publish are separate.

  5. Share on your terms.

    Once the tour is reviewed and sharing is enabled, copy its link or embed code from your desk. Viewers need no account or capture app. Anyone who receives the link can forward it.

Your first session: one practice capture.

For every new account, and for capture partners.

Veylet confirms your device and app access first, and the app unlocks real captures once your practice room passes. Installation alone does not approve you for client work.

  1. Check the device and install the agreed build.With Veylet support, confirm the exact model, rear LiDAR, OS version, camera permission and available storage. Follow the installation link Veylet sends you. If the device is unsupported, stop and agree another device or managed capture.
  2. Record one small, permissioned space.Read the preparation guide, clear private items and follow the current in-app movement prompts. Start with the agreed practice route. Branding, team invitations and website setup can wait.
  3. Inspect what you saved.Open the saved photographs and check coverage before leaving. A saved capture is your first setup checkpoint; it is not a finished or quality-approved tour. Keep the original if you need help or another attempt.
  4. Export, then confirm the handoff.Choose Export capture in the app and save to Files or AirDrop to your Mac. Ask Veylet support for the private transfer route and wait for its receipt. Exporting is not uploading; sending directly from the app is not available in the current release. Veylet processes the capture automatically and an automatic quality check assesses the result. Keep originals until transfer is confirmed. Client work needs explicit production approval and agreed terms.

Stuck at sign-in or transfer? Keep your capture and tell Veylet support which step stopped, the device model and app build. Do not include passwords, access codes or private images in an email. New accounts are admitted in weekly groups from the waitlist; sign in with the email you joined with.

Keep the handover simple.

Already admitted?

Use the email you joined with on both the website and capture app. Sign in, then save a space. Account creation does not grant production approval.

When the listing changes.

Revoke the handoff and remove its embed when the tour should stop being available. Revocation blocks new access; it cannot erase copies already downloaded. Agree hosting dates and any archive or deletion request with Veylet support.

Before you start.

What if the first result is not usable?

An automatic quality check decides whether a tour is ready before it is offered for your approval. If your first walkthrough isn’t listing-ready, we redo it free: the redo corrects it on the same link and uses no walkthrough, though a new capture visit is not included. Keep the originals and report the affected area. After that, we agree a correction, a bounded recapture or the remedy in your scope; we do not treat a failed technical retry as a new tour. Sharing waits for review and approval.

Can every visitor open a tour?

Visitors use a current browser with graphics support on a phone, tablet or computer. Performance depends on the tour, device and connection. Share a direct link as a fallback for website builders that block embedded content. Portal compatibility must be checked with that portal.

Can an agency use it free?

Eligible App Store subscribers, or accounts with an agreed invoiced start, receive 3 free months with 6 accepted walkthroughs in total. They begin when the plan is activated with a payment method on file, and there is one trial per agency (ABN) and workspace. The first charge is on the day they end; cancel before then and nothing is charged. App Store subscriptions renew at the price of the plan you chose, monthly or annual, unless cancelled through Apple. Invoiced service continues only under explicitly agreed and settled terms; it does not auto-renew. On the monthly Veylet plan each paid month includes 2 accepted walkthroughs, and unused ones roll over, up to 4 banked; the annual plan has 24 to use any time in the plan year, and 4 bonus walkthroughs and 4 Super fast renders if you choose it before your free months end. For a busier month the account owner can add a pack of 3 or 10 walkthroughs, valid 12 months, including during the free months. Check the renewal date on your account; you can cancel any time. Every walkthrough you released stays live while your plan runs; when it ends, its links keep working for 14 days, then go offline until you restart it. While capture quality is still being proven we onboard accounts in cohorts, so ask about availability before promising a client a date.

Is a walkthrough a measured survey?

No. It provides visual context for a space. It is not a measured floor plan, building survey or guarantee of condition. Keep listing photography and required property information available alongside it.
